svg.text: Every line verified on the running platform, 24 September 2026, by signing in as that account and trying it.
+ built and seen working ~ partly built - refused, by the database and not by the interface
Runs the restoration. Needs buyers and financing.
+ Create a project: name, location, boundary, catchment
+ Availability: periods, expected, BUFFER, unit type
+ Every figure paired with its source + as-of date
+ See what is still blocking publication
- Publish its own project - only Sylva can
- Edit anything: append-only, an edit is version + 1
Wants units, or the benefit. Asks: is this relevant to me?
+ Register its own sites (factory, brewery, plant)
+ DISTANCE from its sites to each project
+ Read claim rights and what is EXCLUDED
+ Availability per period, with the unit named
+ Ask a PRIVATE question (no public comments exist)
+ Express interest -> deal + permanent record entry
- See another buyer's sites, deals, terms or identity
- Reach the owner, admin or auditor areas
Verified: 23 km and 241 km to the Havel project
A bank or fund. Finances the project, repaid from revenue.
+ FINANCING NEED - nobody else sees this
- Register sites - that is a buyer's feature
- EXPRESS INTEREST - only buyers can create a deal
- Reach the owner, admin or auditor areas
No return, yield or IRR anywhere - not ours to state
RUNS THE PLATFORM, AND CHECKS IT
Sylva itself. Decides who may transact, and what goes public.
+ Every decision needs a written reason
+ Approval is DERIVED from the decision by trigger
+ Publish a project, once the gate passes
+ See real identities behind a pseudonym
- Force publication past the gate - the DB refuses
- Edit or delete a record entry - corrections are NEW rows
For the funder and external audit. Inspects, changes nothing.
- Create a deal or buy a unit
Only button on the page is Sign out. A guard walks every
table and fails if the auditor holds any write privilege.
Discovers projects. The page is shareable and indexable.
+ Read a full project page, all 11 sections
+ See a buyer as 'Buyer 014', with sector and country
- See an unpublished project - returns nothing, not a 403
- See a buyer's real name unless THAT deal was disclosed
NAMED ON THE PLATFORM, BUT NOT USERS OF IT
Checks whether the ecological result meets the scheme's rules.
- Log in - there is no verifier account
- Act on the platform at all
The note defines no verifier workflow, so we invented none
Owns the land. NOT necessarily the one running the project.
+ Named on the project page, separately from the developer
+ A buyer can see who controls the land, and for how long
- Log in - there is no landowner account
- Act on the platform at all
The landowner may be the project owner, or may not be -
the project page names both, separately
reads the financing, may fund it
checks the result on the ground
the scheme issues them, in ITS registry
THE SAME RULE UNDER ALL EIGHT
Role comes from the PostgreSQL role and cannot be forged. Organisation comes from an HMAC-signed context and cannot be forged.
So the screen never decides who sees what - it asks, and the database answers. A buyer asking Postgres directly for another buyer's
sites gets zero rows; for a pseudonym's organisation, "permission denied". Tested as each role, not assumed.
